newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Body parts seen flying in air in Jerusalem carnage.
newsitem.headline: Body parts seen flying in air in Jerusalem carnage.

text.p: First people heard two explosions within seconds of each other. Then they saw body parts flying in the air.
A big fireball and a cloud of smoke filled the crowded street market in the heart of Jewish west Jerusalem on Wednesday.
Israeli police said the blasts, apparently the work of two Arab suicide bombers, killed 18 people including the attackers.
"Peace? Peace? They call this peace?" shrieked a middle-aged Israeli woman observing the carnage and confusion and shaking her hands furiously in the air.
The explosions occurred just as Israel and the Palestinians had been preparing for a U.S. Middle East envoy's mission on Thursday to salvage peacemaking from a four-month-long crisis.
"Death to Arabs," "Kill them all", shouted a few dozen Jewish youths who gathered in the Mahane Yehuda market two hours after the explosions.
Blown-up watermelons and eggplants mingled with blood and body parts along the ground while police, rescue workers and people off the street struggled to remove the dead and treat the wounded.
"There were two large explosions and then I saw body parts flying in the air. There was a big fireball right in my face," one witness said.
Police swiftly closed the market to search through garbage bins and debris for any more bombs.
One man in his early 30s who appeared to be paralysed, a market butcher in his smock and rubber boots, lay on the sidewalk on a stretcher as bystanders pleaded for help.
"Why don't they take him? Where is a doctor?" one woman shouted.
A bearded ultra-Orthodox Jew and a journalist picked up the stretcher and plunged into the chaos of medical crews to find an ambulance.
The blast touched both Jews and Arabs who work side by side at food stands in the narrow alleyways of the partly covered market. People's skin was scorched black.

"I heard a huge boom. Two seconds later there was a second boom, just as strong if not stronger. There were people all over the ground -- Arabs, Jews. Police came, ambulances. My God," said Samir Salah Daoud Joumhour, a 15-year-old Arab worker.
Bearded ultra-Orthodox Jews collected pieces of flesh and bone for burial as required by religious law.
An ultra-Orthodox Jew named Micha searched his memory for a relevant explanation from the Bible.
"Esau envied Jacob. Ishmael was jealous of Isaac. Arabs hate the Jews, the Jews are God's chosen people, and this is the result," the man said.
